proposal.name: provider_attribute_join_validation
proposal.trigger: Before using provider-level attributes (specialty, network status, group affiliation) in claims analysis, especially when joining claims to a provider directory
proposal.objective: Verify complete and correct matching of claims to the provider directory before using provider attributes in analysis, preventing silent data loss, undetected mismatches, and downstream analysis errors
procedure: Identify the claim table, the provider key column to be used (e.g., rendering_npi or billing_npi), and the provider directory table with its candidate key (e.g., provider_npi)
Configure a join_check component to test the cardinality and matching coverage of the claim.provider_key -> provider.provider_key relationship
Set the validate parameter to 'many_to_one' to assert each claim maps to at most one provider record
Execute the join check and inspect the results: cardinality, rows_left, rows_after_inner_join, unmatched_left count, unmatched_left_denominator, and right_key_unique flag
Verify that unmatched_left equals zero and right_key_unique is true, confirming complete coverage and a valid many-to-one relationship
Document the join check results in the output metrics, including the row counts and cardinality, before proceeding to group or filter by provider attributes
Only use provider attributes in downstream analysis after confirming unmatched_left == 0 (zero unmatched claims)
required_checks: Join cardinality is verified and recorded as many_to_one
Unmatched rows on the left (claims) side equals zero
Provider key uniqueness is confirmed (right_key_unique = true)
Join check results (including unmatched counts and cardinality) are included in output before downstream analysis uses provider attributes
expected_artifacts: join_check results with fields: cardinality, rows_left, rows_after_inner_join, unmatched_left, unmatched_left_denominator, right_key_unique
failure_modes: Unmatched claims due to NPI encoding differences, stale provider directory, or data quality issues remain silent and are dropped in inner joins
Many-to-many relationships (right_key_unique = false) indicate duplicate or composite provider records, inflating or duplicating claim-level metrics
Incomplete provider directory coverage causes systematic bias by excluding certain provider types or categories from analysis
